Represent sampled video images and text in a shared numerical space for local visual search.

## Current availability {#current-availability}

Desktop builds package the required onnxruntime-node 1.29.0 engine for macOS arm64, Linux arm64, Linux x64, Windows x64. Install this model’s weights through Model Manager, then run its task locally. These are supported build targets; consult the nightly test report for results on a particular package and machine. The desktop build does not package this engine for macOS x64 even though model weights are listed for those platforms.

## Use this model {#use-this-model}

Open **Framescaper: Tools → Search → Index Video, then Tools → Search → Indexed Search** on a platform with the required native runtime. Local assistance runs in the desktop editor.

1. Select video and install SigLIP2 through Manage Models.
2. Run Index Video to analyze sampled frames. Install PP-OCRv4 too if you want its optional text-reading step.
3. Use Indexed Search and review the matching video moments before deciding how to use them.

## Download and requirements {#download-and-requirements}

Model identity: `siglip2-base-patch16-224`, version **2.0.0**.

Approximate download size: **393.25 MiB**. Minimum system memory: **8 GiB**. This catalog requirement refers to total memory, not currently free memory. Inference also needs sufficient free memory, and installation needs working space; memory is not a speed guarantee.

Published platforms: macOS arm64, macOS x64, Linux arm64, Linux x64, Windows x64. A matching packaged runtime is also required.

On Windows, install the latest supported [Microsoft Visual C++ v14 Redistributable](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170) matching the desktop app: **x64** for an x64 build or **ARM64** for an ARM64 build. The native ONNX and Sherpa engines require these libraries; model downloads do not include them. Visual Studio itself is not required to use the app.

Tools → Model Manager downloads the published artifacts and verifies their recorded SHA-256 digests. Processing uses the installed files locally. Open Storage and verification in Model Manager to inspect notices, repair an installation, or change the storage location.

| Artifact | Approximate download size |
| --- | --- |
| vision_model_int8.onnx | 90.17 MiB |
| text_model_int8.onnx | 270.31 MiB |
| tokenizer.json | 32.77 MiB |
| config.json | 435 bytes |
| preprocessor_config.json | 394 bytes |

## What the packaged test checks {#what-the-packaged-test-checks}

Case: `siglip-image-text-embedding`; operation: `image-text-embedding`.

Input: Two photographs: the public-domain NASA portrait of astronaut Eileen Collins and the CC0 Chelsea cat photograph. Each is fitted into a separate frame with explicit source-frame timing, giving the detectors a human face and a clear object.

Embedding vectors must have the expected dimensions and contain finite, nonzero, nonconstant values.

The nightly-with-tests package downloads real model artifacts and requests inference through the packaged runtime. A required model missing from the signed catalog fails its case. Missing native engines fail on catalog-supported platforms. These costly checks run separately from the normal browser suite. A passing run confirms basic model execution and usable output structure; it does not establish perceptual quality or accuracy on your recording.

## Review the result {#review-the-result}

- This model produces embeddings, not captions or an authoritative description of every frame.
- The packaged test uses frame input and text tag prototypes, exercising both the image and text networks. It checks valid vectors rather than an exact ranking.
